findings.title: Startup index build drops writes committed while indexes are being built
findings.body: The indexes are populated from ListIterator snapshots before the write-event watch is opened. The SQL WatchWriteEvents implementation initializes its cursor from the latest resource versions at subscription time, so any write committed after an index's list snapshot but before this call is treated as already seen and is never sent to handleEvent. In HA deployments, writes from another server during startup can therefore leave added documents missing, modified documents stale, or deleted documents searchable until another relevant write occurs. Start/buffer the watch before building, or replay events from the resource version returned by each build.

findings.title: Closing a backend watch channel can panic the server during shutdown
findings.body: This receive does not check the channel's ok result before dereferencing v. A normal backend shutdown closes its event channel (the SQL poller closes its stream), after which this loop receives a nil *WrittenEvent and panics while evaluating v.Type. Stop invokes Lifecycle.Stop before s.cancel, and this PR now starts initWatcher during every ResourceServer construction, so even servers that never serve a request can hit this shutdown crash. Exit the loop when the channel is closed and make the loop observe cancellation.

findings.title: The eagerly started search watcher panics when its event stream closes
findings.body: The search watcher also receives from events without checking whether the channel was closed. On normal SQL backend shutdown the poller closes the stream, causing v to be nil and handleEvent to dereference it. This is now started during construction whenever search is configured, and it uses context.Background(), so server cancellation does not stop it. Check the receive ok value and use a server-owned cancellable context for the watcher.

findings.title: Parallel index workers race on totalBatchesIndexed
findings.body: errgroup runs these functions concurrently when WorkerThreads is greater than one, but each one increments the shared totalBatchesIndexed integer without synchronization. This is a Go data race, causes race-detector failures, and can emit an incorrect tracing count. Use an atomic counter or collect per-worker results after the group completes.

findings.title: Failed eager initialization leaves partially started resources running
findings.body: If search.init succeeds and starts its watch goroutine but initWatcher subsequently fails, NewResourceServer returns an error without calling cancel or Lifecycle.Stop. No ResourceServer is returned to the caller, so it cannot later be stopped; the search watcher is particularly leaked because it was created with context.Background(). Ensure constructor failure cleans up the server context and any successfully initialized lifecycle resources before returning the error.
